title: The Signal Tower

beats.narrativeText: With most of Outpost Echo humming again, Atlas points to the one structure still standing dark: the Signal Tower.
This wasn't a system that failed on its own — the original expedition shut it down deliberately. Nothing recovered so far says why.
The learner inspects the tower's systems in detail, cataloguing multiple engineering faults rather than assuming there's just one.
Diagnosing each fault properly reveals just how many separate problems have to be solved, in the right order, before the tower can safely transmit at all.
The learner must develop a full repair sequence — deciding which faults matter most to fix first, with no single correct answer handed to them.
Testing and refining one fault at a time, the learner brings the tower back online — the first time in the whole campaign they've carried a multi-stage engineering problem from start to finish alone.
The learner records the design decisions made throughout the repair, aware this is the most independent engineering work the campaign has asked of them yet.

Long-range communications finally come back online. And buried in what the tower can now reach is something nobody expected: the expedition built this, believing someone would come looking for them one day.

activities.title: Inspect Tower Systems
activities.storyContext: The Signal Tower was intentionally shut down by the original expedition — this wasn't neglect, it was a decision.
activities.instructions: Inspect the tower's systems carefully and note anything that looks damaged or disconnected, without assuming you've found the only problem yet.
activities.output: A list of observed issues with the tower's systems.

activities.title: Identify Faults
activities.storyContext: Before the tower can safely transmit, every fault has to be properly diagnosed — not guessed at.
activities.instructions: Diagnose the specific engineering faults preventing the tower from working, one at a time.

activities.title: Develop a Repair Sequence
activities.storyContext: This is the learner's first multi-stage engineering investigation — nobody is going to hand over a single prescribed order to follow.
activities.instructions: Decide the order in which the faults should be repaired, and be ready to explain why that order and not another.

activities.title: Test and Refine Solutions
activities.storyContext: Each repair must be tested before moving on to the next.
activities.instructions: Test each proposed solution and refine it if it doesn't fully solve the fault.
activities.output: Tested and refined solutions for each fault.

activities.title: Record Design Decisions
activities.storyContext: A good engineer can always explain why they made the choices they did — not just that the tower works now.
activities.instructions: Record the design decisions made throughout the repair, and the reasoning behind each one.
activities.output: A written record of design decisions.

activities.title: Compare Alternative Repair Strategies
activities.storyContext: There is often more than one way to solve an engineering problem.
activities.instructions: Compare a couple of alternative repair strategies and justify the one you chose.
activities.output: A comparison of alternative repair strategies with a justified choice.

activities.title: Communication Towers in Remote Environments
activities.storyContext: Outpost Echo's Signal Tower faces the same challenges as real communication towers in remote places.
activities.instructions: Find out how communication towers operate in remote environments.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What was the hardest fault to fix, and what made it harder than the others?

discussionPoints: Why was it important to fix the faults in a particular order?
What did testing reveal that planning alone couldn't?
parentGuide.preparation: Simple building or craft materials are useful if the learner wants to model any part of the tower.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a repair sequence that is justified by reasoning, and evidence of testing and refinement across multiple faults.

completionCriteria: Tower faults identified, a repair sequence developed, and solutions tested and refined.
